figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Teaser. L3G-World generates an explorable, spatially consistent world in real time from a single image and a camera trajectory. To this end, L3G-Mem maintains a latent 3D Gaussian memory, and L3G-Gen generates video conditioned on VAE latents rendered from the memory.
figures.headline: L3G-World generates an explorable, spatially consistent world in real time from one image and a camera trajectory.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: L3G-Mem. (a) L3G-Mem takes the current window $\mathcal{W}_{k}$ and the memory $\mathcal{M}_{k-1}$. Rendering $\mathcal{M}_{k-1}$ into the current cameras determines which geometry features are clustered by K-means into spawning queries, and identifies the visible Gaussians whose memory tokens are retrieved as refinement tokens. Both token sets are jointly processed by a transformer and decoded into new Gaussians and residual updates, respectively. (b) Given the input video chunk, RGB and opacity rendered from the previous memory identify regions requiring new Gaussians through a spawning mask. As a result, the updated memory can fully reconstruct the observed scene.
figures.headline: The memory updater spawns new Gaussians in regions the memory does not cover and refines the visible ones.
citing_sentences: As illustrated in Fig. 2, L3G-World realizes these decisions with two modules that alternate autoregressively: a memory updater, L3G-Mem, which reads and updates the latent 3D Gaussian memory with each generated chunk, and a video generator, L3G-Gen, which generates the next chunk conditioned on the memory rendered in its latent space.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: L3G-Gen. (a) L3G-Gen renders the VAE latents and opacity of the 3D memory to the target cameras, concatenates them with the noisy latents along the channel dimension, and generates the next chunk conditioned on the history latents. (b) We visualize the ground-truth and generated video, with target-view rendered VAE condition from the latent 3D Gaussian memory, illustrating that spatially aligned latent memory provides consistent conditioning for video generation.
figures.headline: Rendered VAE latents from the memory align with target views and condition generation of the next chunk.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: L3G-World Pipeline. L3G-World couples video generation and memory updating in a chunk-wise loop, where each generated chunk updates the persistent 3D memory, which in turn conditions subsequent chunk generation.
figures.headline: Video generation and memory updating alternate chunk by chunk, with each update conditioning the next chunk.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Qualitative results of L3G-World. (a) L3G-Mem corrects geometric errors in the 3D memory through residual refinement using video chunks generated by L3G-Gen. (b) L3G-World maintains scene consistency over long-horizon generation through its persistent 3D memory. (c) Rendering the memory’s VAE features from target camera views provides spatially aligned conditioning, enabling consistent video generation along diverse camera trajectories.
figures.headline: Residual refinement corrects memory geometry, and rendered VAE features keep generated video consistent across camera trajectories.

abstract: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. Existing approaches rely on either temporal context or explicit 3D memory, both of which scale poorly because memory grows with the length of the generated stream. Moreover, explicit 3D memories condition latent video generators by re-encoding RGB renderings, which precludes real-time generation. In this paper, we introduce a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory (L3G) that combines the efficiency of feed-forward reconstruction with a compact, rapidly renderable scene representation. Building on this memory, we propose L3G-World, in which a memory updater and a video diffusion transformer (DiT) alternate autoregressively to generate spatially consistent worlds. The memory updater spawns Gaussians in newly observed regions and refines existing ones, so that the memory grows with scene extent rather than stream length. Each Gaussian further stores a VAE latent feature, allowing the memory to be rendered directly into the DiT’s latent space without VAE re-encoding. Experiments show that L3G-World achieves state-of-the-art results on generation quality and long-horizon self-consistency, with up to $38.6\times$ fewer 3D primitives, $3.2\times$ faster memory reconstruction, and $359\times$ faster VAE feature rendering relative to the most efficient prior 3D-memory baseline for each metric, enabling real-time world generation at 9 FPS.

sections.body: The section argues that temporal-context methods grow in memory and attention cost with stream length, as shown in Tab. 1. It also argues that dense feed-forward 3D memories accumulate redundant primitives, while optimization-based 3D memories are too slow for real-time use. It proposes L3G-World. A feed-forward memory updater, L3G-Mem, spawns Gaussians only in uncovered regions and refines existing ones. A memory-conditioned video diffusion transformer, L3G-Gen, is conditioned on VAE latents rendered directly from the memory. Against the most efficient prior 3D-memory baseline for each metric, the reported gains are 26.7–38.9× fewer 3D primitives, 3.0–3.2× faster memory reconstruction, and 349–359× higher VAE-space rendering throughput. Real-time generation runs at 9.02 FPS on one H100 GPU.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Interactive world models face a cost-consistency trade-off, and a compact latent Gaussian memory is proposed to address it.

sections.body: The related work covers video diffusion with few-step, causal generation for streaming, and interactive world models that condition on user actions. Feed-forward 3D reconstruction predicts per-pixel point maps or Gaussians, and streaming variants process images online. Consistent world generation uses explicit point-cloud or Gaussian memories. Feed-forward versions keep adding primitives, so memory and rendering cost grow with the generation horizon. Optimization-based memories keep a scene-level representation but incur substantial latency. L3G-World keeps compact 3D Gaussians and stores VAE latent features in each one. Table 1 reports L3G-World at 7.4 GiB peak GPU memory and 9.02 total FPS, and it is the only method marked real-time.
sections.heading: Related Works
sections.headline: Prior explicit 3D memories either accumulate dense per-frame primitives or optimize too slowly for real-time generation.

sections.body: L3G-Mem updates the memory once per input window: $\mathcal{M}_{k}=\operatorname{Update}\left(\mathcal{M}_{k-1},\mathcal{W}_{k}\right)$. Pixels with low opacity or high RGB error under the rendered memory form a spawn mask. K-means over geometry features inside that mask yields spawning queries, and visible Gaussians supply refinement tokens. One transformer processes both token sets. New Gaussians are appended, and retrieved Gaussians receive residual updates. Latent-lifting queries are concatenated with spawn tokens so each Gaussian carries a VAE feature. L3G-Gen, a video diffusion transformer fine-tuned with LoRA, is trained with rectified flow on rendered memory latents and opacity. A few-step student is then distilled with AnyFlow and on-policy distribution matching. Stop gradients through the previous memory keep training causal.
sections.heading: Methodology
sections.headline: A memory updater spawns Gaussians in uncovered regions, refines existing ones, and renders VAE latent features directly into the generator.

sections.body: Experiments start from a single image and use 481-frame loop-closure trajectories. Self-consistency is scored by PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS between outgoing and returning views. Generation quality uses LPIPS, FID and four VBench metrics. Camera error uses TransErr and RotErr, and geometry uses MEt3R. Baselines include point-cloud, Gaussian and temporal-context methods, all evaluated on one A100 GPU. In Table 2 on the first dataset, L3G-World reports 33 K primitives, 11.88 MiB memory, 40.088 reconstruction FPS, and 1,086.58 VAE-space render FPS. The distilled L3G-World Fast variant reports 70 K primitives and 25.55 MiB. The ablation in Table 4 shows that removing memory refinement lowers all reported metrics. Table 3 shows that removing adaptive spawning uses 1.8× more Gaussians.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On the first of two datasets, L3G-World reaches the highest loop-closure PSNR, 16.00, among the compared methods.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the design. A feed-forward updater spawns Gaussians only in insufficiently covered regions and refines existing ones. Each Gaussian carries a VAE-space feature, so memory renders into the DiT latent space without re-encoding. The authors state that L3G-World achieves leading generation quality for long-horizon spatial consistency while reducing the cost of memory reconstruction, rendering and storage. They present compact latent 3D memory as a practical foundation for scalable interactive world models. The conclusion does not repeat the limitations listed in the appendix.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion presents compact latent 3D memory as a practical foundation for scalable interactive world models.

sections.body: The appendix gives background on flow maps, average velocity and on-policy distillation, and on 3D Gaussian splatting. Implementation details cover the updater architecture, with geometry features taken from layers 39, 29 and 19 and 128-dimensional VAE tokens. They also cover the spawn mask, built from patch MSE and accumulated alpha, and visibility thresholds of 0.05 and 1/255. Table 5 lists training steps and parameter counts. Table 6 reports online reconstruction on DL3DV, where L3G-Mem uses 39 primitives (K) and 14.11 MiB. The stated limitations are that the method targets static scenes, that memory can still grow under very large exploration, and that errors can propagate through long autoregressive generation.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix gives flow-map and Gaussian preliminaries, training and retrieval details, online reconstruction results, and limitations.
